name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+25 partisan lean makes this one of the most Republican seats in the country
Tom Sell has raised $2.1 million plus $1.3 million in outside support; Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000
Prediction markets price the Republican at 99 percent
Open seat removes incumbency but does not threaten Republican hold
model.rationale: The R+25 lean alone points to a roughly 25-point Republican edge, and every other signal agrees: Sell has outspent Rable by more than 60-to-1 with heavy outside backing, and markets give the Democrat a one percent chance. An open seat offers no realistic opening in terrain this red.
model.watch: A late scandal or unexpected Democratic outside spending could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
West Texas's 19th District is among the most Republican seats in the nation, with a partisan lean of R+25, and Representative Jodey Arrington's retirement does little to change that. Tom Sell enters the general election as the clear favorite, backed by more than $2.1 million in fundraising and roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $31,000 with no outside help.

Prediction markets give the Republican a 99 percent chance of holding the seat, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The expected margin is around 20 points Republican, with the outcome all but certain; the only real question is the size of the victory, not which party wins.
